resources.string: No syncs yet.\n\nConnect at least one service in Accounts (or use CSV files), then tap + to create your first sync.
The service is limiting requests: resuming in %1$d s. Normal with large playlists, not an error.
Leave empty to use the source playlist’s name.
Remove from the target every track that is not in the source, including tracks added there by hand. Off = only add.
After adding, the target is put in the source’s order. Spotify, YouTube Music and Deezer can do it.
How a track is chosen among the candidates. The defaults suit most syncs.
Strict accepts fewer automatic matches and sends more to review; loose the opposite.
A candidate from another album (single, compilation, reissue) loses much more ground.
Never a live, remix, acoustic or karaoke version in place of one that is not.
Connect at least one service in the Accounts tab first.
Choose a source playlist and a target.
Trackhop ships without service keys. Create your own free key on the service\'s developer page: it takes about two minutes and the app guides you step by step.
Requires a Spotify account. Playlists and Liked Songs.

YouTube Music playlists and likes through the web player\'s own interface, built into this version: sign in with your Google account, no Google Cloud project, no quota. Not an official Google API: read the notice shown before signing in.
Install the companion app "Trackhop Bridge" from GitHub, then come back here and press Connect. Prefer the official route? Use the "YouTube Music (Google API)" card below.
Official YouTube Data API with a Google Cloud project of your own. Daily quota is limited: large syncs may take several days.
Tracks not found on the target
Show a notification when a scheduled sync adds or removes tracks, and when any sync fails.

When a track carries no ISRC (web routes, files), Trackhop looks it up once in Deezer\'s public catalogue, so Spotify, Apple Music and TIDAL answer with the exact recording instead of a look-alike. Anonymous request, no account involved.
Trackhop follows the system language: English, Italian, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean.

Trackhop ships without keys of its own: the official routes of Spotify, YouTube, TIDAL, Deezer, Last.fm and Apple Music use a free key created in your name, so their limits and quotas are yours alone. Here you can see and change them.
Connections log, technical report to share, traffic capture for the web connectors. Off, they stay out of the way.

Trackhop is free with no subscriptions. It is supported by a single small banner ad; no data is sold, and apart from the ad, nothing leaves your phone except the requests to the music services you connect.
File playlists live inside the app. Import a file here, then use it as a sync source; or sync any playlist into a file and export it as CSV or M3U.
Saved inside Trackhop: use “Save as file” here, or Tools › File playlists, to get a CSV or M3U.
Security check failed (state mismatch). Please try again.
The playlists on the services are not touched. Both halves of a two-way sync are deleted, and tracks you chose to ignore stay ignored.
Source playlist is empty: nothing to do (removals skipped for safety).
Apple Music playlists in your library. Needs a subscription and a MusicKit developer token. Apple\'s API can add tracks but not remove them.

Local files: import a playlist you exported from any service (CSV, M3U, Apple Music/iTunes XML, JSON, or a plain list) and sync it anywhere. The bridge for services with no open API: Amazon Music, Qobuz, SoundCloud.
No Apple Music developer token yet. Enter yours from Accounts, Apple Music, Set up.
%1$s: the library needs an active Apple Music subscription; Apple refused (403: %2$s).
Link not recognised. Supported: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube/YouTube Music, Deezer, TIDAL.
The tracks the AI proposed are kept in the file “%1$s”. To add more, use “Extend with AI” in the sync’s menu.
Connect %1$s first to read this link.
%1$s does not allow removing tracks from a playlist via its API: %2$d tracks were left in place.
Removals postponed: the search was not completed, so %1$d tracks in the target that matched nothing yet were left in place. They will be reviewed when a run completes.

Removals held back: this run would remove %1$d of the %2$d tracks in the target. Tap the sync\'s status to open the preview and see them; if they really should go, tick “Remove these tracks” there and run it. If the source has not really lost them, the service listed it incompletely and nothing should go.
Nothing changed on either side since the last run: skipped.

%1$d of %2$d tracks searched, then the service asked for a longer pause (%3$s). This is a limit of the service, not a Trackhop error: what was found has been applied and remembered. Run the sync again in a few minutes to continue from there.
%1$s cannot remove tracks from a playlist
%1$s can only add tracks: removals will be skipped.
Redirect URI to paste in the dashboard
Spotify requires an app registered in your name. It is free; an app in Development Mode serves up to 5 accounts, plenty for personal use.
Google requires a Cloud project in your name to use the YouTube API. It is free and the daily quota is yours alone.
TIDAL requires an app registered in your name. It is free.
Deezer needs an app registered in your name. The https redirect page is provided by the project.
The developer token belongs to your Apple Developer account and expires after six months at most.
%1$s only allows a handful of users per app. Set up your own credentials: it is free and takes about two minutes.
the phone could not reach the service (DNS failed). Check the connection, any VPN or private DNS, and that Trackhop is allowed to use data in the background, then try again.
no answer from the browser, time is up

This would remove %1$d of the %2$d tracks in the target. Check that the source really lists that few: an incomplete listing by the service looks exactly like this. Unless you tick the box below, the run adds tracks and keeps these.
The target playlist will be created.
Nothing to do: the playlists are in sync.
Accept a proposal with one tap, or open a track to search %1$s. Every choice is remembered for the next syncs.
The sync is still adding the tracks it found. You can already fix these.
Title, “artist - title”, or the link of the track

This link is not a %1$s track

Imported lists and playlists a sync wrote to “File”: import, paste, export.
Describe a playlist; your own AI writes it, Trackhop finds the tracks.
Every playlist, liked song, album and artist of this service saved as dated files.

Spotify refused the request (%1$s). Apps in Development Mode cannot read playlists made by Spotify itself (Discover Weekly, Release Radar, editorial mixes) and only serve accounts listed in the app\'s User Management. Pick a playlist you or another user created, or add the account on developer.spotify.com.
Spotify refused the request (%1$s): this permission was added after you connected. Reconnect Spotify in Accounts and it will be granted.

Spotify refused the request: the account that created the key has no active Premium, and since February 2026 Spotify switches a developer app off without it (after a subscription change it can take a few hours). Use the "Spotify (web)" route instead, or a key created by a Premium account that lists you among its users.
Spotify is asking to slow down: too many requests in a short time. Try again in %1$s.
Save any playlist of this service as a file on your phone (CSV, M3U, XSPF, JSPF or plain text), without changing anything on the service.

Saves every playlist (and your liked songs) as files in the Files screen, ready to export as CSV or M3U. Each run adds a dated version; the last %1$d versions of each playlist are kept, and a playlist that has not changed is not written again. Nothing is changed on the service.
Finds tracks that appear twice in a playlist, even with a different ID or version, and keeps the first copy.
Copy, merge, split, sort or shuffle playlists. The result is always a new playlist on this service; the originals are not touched.
Pick several playlists of one service and send them all to another: one sync each, created and run one after the other. They stay in Syncs, so you can run them again or schedule them.
%1$d syncs created and started: follow them in Syncs.

Describe the playlist you want and your own AI writes it; Trackhop then looks the tracks up on the service you choose, like a normal sync, so anything the AI got wrong ends up among the tracks to review. Trackhop has no AI of its own: you connect yours (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible server, even a local one) with a key from your account, and only the text you type here is sent to it.
Created in your account on the provider\'s site; it stays on this phone, encrypted.
No model found with this key.
What do you want to listen to?
e.g. Italian indie for a summer road trip, upbeat, mostly after 2010
One track per line, as “Artist – Title”
Up to about 100 fits in one answer; more is asked in rounds.
Above 100 the model is asked in rounds and uses more tokens: for large numbers check your AI plan\'s token allowance first.
The AI returned no tracks. Try a more precise description.
%1$d tracks proposed: the sync towards %2$s has started, follow it in Syncs.
%1$d tracks in “%2$s” on %3$s. The sync keeps the list and the playlist paired.
Your key and model for the playlist generator in Tools.
Remove what you do not want, then confirm: the tracks will be looked up on %1$s and anything not found will be there to review.

Free to try: Google Gemini and Groq have a free tier, OpenRouter has free models (the ones ending in “:free”). A key takes a minute on the provider\'s site. Trackhop cannot ship a shared key: it would be visible in the open source code and used up within a day.
The AI gets the same description and the tracks already in the playlist, and proposes new ones to add.
%1$d tracks added: the sync has started.
The source playlist “%1$s” no longer exists on %2$s. Edit the sync and pick another.
The target playlist “%1$s” no longer exists on %2$s. Edit the sync: create it again or pick another.
Say what to add, or leave it empty to continue in the spirit of the tracks already there. The AI proposes, you review, and only what %1$s actually has is added.
e.g. more 90s trip hop, nothing after 2005
%1$s does not allow renaming or deleting playlists from other apps.
Your playlists on this service in one list: rename or delete them where the service allows it, or export them.

Reads every playlist of this service once and shows the tracks that sit in more than one, and the liked songs that are in no playlist. Nothing is changed. On YouTube it costs quota like a full backup.
%1$d playlists read · %2$d tracks in several playlists · %3$d liked songs in none
Every track is in one playlist at most, and every liked song is in a playlist.
Delete “%1$s” from %2$s? This cannot be undone.
No playlists of yours on this service.

resources.string: Pick a folder (SD card, Nextcloud, Drive, any app that offers one) and Trackhop saves dated backups of your playlists there, so they survive the phone. Nothing is saved until a backup runs: on the schedule below, or with Copy now. To restore, import a file from that folder in Files.
Copy now first backs up every connected service, then copies the files not yet in the folder.
%1$d services backed up, %2$d new files copied
The backup folder can no longer be reached: it was deleted, the card was removed or the app lost access to it. Choose a folder again.
Some phones (Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Samsung) stop background apps. Exclude Trackhop from battery optimisation so the schedule is respected.
Link received: choose where to sync it.
The shared text has no recognisable playlist link.
Setlist imported: %1$d songs. Choose where to create the playlist.
Connector in beta: it works, but it has seen less use than the others. If something goes wrong, please report it.
Your own music server: Navidrome, Airsonic, Gonic, LMS, Funkwhale and anything speaking the Subsonic API. No registration, no quota. Starred songs count as liked songs.
Your Jellyfin server. No registration, no quota. Favourites count as liked songs.
Your Plex Media Server, with your X-Plex-Token. Music playlists are read, created and updated on the server.
Loved tracks of a Last.fm profile, as a source only. Needs a free Last.fm API key.
Playlists and loved tracks of a ListenBrainz user. With your user token, loved tracks can also be written (liked songs as target).
Your credentials stay encrypted on this phone. Trackhop only talks to the server you enter here.

Enter the address of your Navidrome, Airsonic or other Subsonic-compatible server (for example https://music.example.com), your username and password. The password is never sent as-is: each request uses a salted hash. Ampache: use the Subsonic password or API key set in Preferences → Account, not your account password.
Enter the address of your Jellyfin server (for example https://jellyfin.example.com), your username and password.

Enter the address of your Plex Media Server (for example http://192.168.1.10:32400) and your X-Plex-Token. Plex explains how to find the token in its support pages ("Finding an authentication token").
Enter the Last.fm username whose loved tracks you want to read. The profile must be public.
Enter the ListenBrainz username whose playlists and loved tracks you want to read. Add your user token (listenbrainz.org → Settings) to also write loved tracks.
ListenBrainz needs your user token to write loved tracks: add it in Accounts (listenbrainz.org → Settings).
ListenBrainz did not accept this token.
Last.fm needs a free API key, issued instantly, to read public profiles.
%1$s is read-only: it can only be a source.
%1$s cannot create playlists from the app: create it in %1$s and pick it here.
You will sign in on %1$s, in your browser. Trackhop never sees your password.
You will sign in on %1$s\'s own page, shown inside the app. Trackhop never sees your password, only the session it leaves.
You will sign in with your Apple ID in Apple\'s own window. Trackhop never sees your password.
Your server details stay encrypted on this phone. Trackhop only talks to your server.
Trackhop only receives a limited, revocable permission, stored encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore).
There is no Trackhop server: data travels only between this phone and %1$s.
You can revoke at any time: here with Disconnect, or from your %1$s account.
No results at all on the service
No results for a well-known track
One call per step. A failure here is the first thing to report.
Delete the syncs using this account first.
Tap + to add a service: Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL, files… You can add several connectors of the same service, each with its own name and account.
Some services can be reached two ways. Easiest: sign in on the site, nothing to create. Official: the service\'s own API with a free key of yours, more stable.

You sign in on the service\'s own page, as you would in a browser: Trackhop never sees your password, it only keeps the session, encrypted on this phone. Nothing to create. Not an official interface: it can stop working when the site changes.

You sign in on the service\'s own page, as in a browser: Trackhop never sees your password, only the session, encrypted on this phone. No official API exists: it can stop working when the site changes.
Your own free API key, created on the service\'s developer page in about two minutes. Official and stable.

Your own free API key, created on developer.spotify.com in about two minutes. Official and stable. Spotify only lets Premium accounts create it (a Spotify rule since February 2026): without Premium, "Web API" stays greyed out there.
A developer token from an Apple Developer account (paid). Official.
Your own Google Cloud key (free, a few minutes). Official, but the daily quota is small: big syncs take days.
Your own free API key. Read-only: a source for playlists and loved tracks.
Your own server: address, user and password.
The browser may already be signed in to another %1$s account. On the sign-in page choose “Not you?” or switch account, then continue with the account for this connector.
Amazon has no open API: Trackhop uses the web player\'s interface, so it can stop working when Amazon changes it. Playlists, search, create, add and remove are supported.
Install or update the companion app \"Trackhop Bridge\" (1.3.1 or newer) from GitHub, then come back here and tap Connect.

Sign in on Spotify\'s own page, no developer app to create. Uses the web player\'s session: not an official route, against Spotify\'s terms, may stop working. The official route with your own key stays available as \"Spotify\".

Sign in with your Apple ID, no Apple Developer Program needed. Uses the web player\'s tokens: not an official route, against Apple\'s terms, may stop working. The official route with your own developer token stays available as \"Apple Music\".
Install or update the companion app \"Trackhop Bridge\" (1.2 or newer) from GitHub, then come back here and tap Connect.
Passwords are typed on the services\' own pages, never in Trackhop.
Trackhop keeps only revocable access tokens, encrypted with the Android Keystore.
There is no Trackhop server and no account to create: nothing leaves your phone except requests to the services you connect.
Disconnecting deletes the token from the phone; every service also lets you revoke it from your account page.
It is stored on this phone only, encrypted with the Android Keystore, like the tokens of your music services.

It leaves the phone only towards %1$s, with each request you make. Trackhop has no server of its own: Settings › Advanced › Show developer tools › Show connections lists every host this app has ever contacted, so you can check.
“Forget the key” deletes it at once. Safer still: create a key just for Trackhop, with a spending limit, and revoke it whenever you like.
Every host this app has contacted since it was installed, and how often. Only the host name is recorded, never what was sent.
The web connectors (YouTube Music, Amazon Music, the web sign-ins) also talk through the browser engine, which does not appear here.
Fingerprint, face or phone PIN before Trackhop opens.
No screen lock is set up on this phone.
Unlock with fingerprint, face or PIN
%1$d removed tracks were restored by hand.
Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Trackhop. Resets at midnight Pacific time. A search costs 100 units, adding a track 50.
Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Trackhop, shared by everyone using the built-in key: what other users consume is not counted here. Your own credentials give you a quota of your own.
This sync will use about %1$s units.
This sync needs about %1$s units, but only %2$s remain today: it will finish over the next days.
Also creates the reverse sync (marked ↔), so tracks added on either side reach the other. Neither removes tracks. Both are edited here.
Available with an existing target playlist and a writable source.
Not with a public link or someone else\'s playlist as source: it can be read, not written.
Copy your playlists from one music service to another and keep them up to date, by hand or on a schedule. Free, no subscription, no account to create.
Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, TIDAL, Deezer, your own server, or a file.
Pick a source playlist and a target. Preview shows exactly what will change before anything happens.
Every hour, day or week. Tracks that cannot be matched are listed so you can fix them yourself.
You sign in on each service\'s own page. Trackhop keeps only an encrypted, revocable token on this phone and has no server of its own.

Trackhop ships without service keys of its own. Where a service\'s official route needs one, you create a free key on its developer page, and the app walks you through it in about two minutes. Your data then flows only between your phone and the service.
One track per line, as \"Artist - Title\", or a setlist.fm link. Numbers at the start of lines are ignored.
Shown while a manual sync is running.
Last sync and a "Sync all" button.

string-array.name: setup_steps_spotify
string-array.item: Sign in at developer.spotify.com with the Spotify account you use every day. Spotify requires that account to have Premium; if you are asked to accept the developer terms, accept them. If "Web API" is greyed out on that page, the account has no Premium: Spotify does not allow the key, use the other route instead.
Press "Create app". Name and description are up to you (for example "Trackhop"). Leave "Website" empty.
In "Redirect URIs" paste exactly the address shown below and press "Add". Without it the login cannot come back to the app.
Under "Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?" tick "Web API", accept the terms and press "Save".
Open the app you created, press "Settings" (top right) and copy the "Client ID" here. You do not need the Client secret.
Optional: "User Management" lets you add up to 5 other Spotify accounts (name and e-mail) that may use your key, for example family members.

string-array.name: setup_steps_youtube
string-array.item: Sign in to console.cloud.google.com with your Google account and create a project. Any name works, for example "Trackhop". Wait for the notification that it has been created, then select it.
Enable the YouTube Data API v3: the link opens its page in the library, press "Enable".
Google Auth Platform, "Overview", press "Get started": app name "Trackhop", your e-mail as support address, audience "External", your e-mail as contact. Accept and press "Create".
Google Auth Platform, "Audience": under "Test users" press "Add users" and add your own Gmail address, then Save. Without this step Google refuses the login with "access blocked".

Google Auth Platform, "Clients", "Create client": application type "Desktop app", any name. Copy the Client ID and the Client secret here. Nothing else to register: the app receives the login on 127.0.0.1.

string-array.name: setup_steps_tidal
string-array.item: Sign in at developer.tidal.com with your TIDAL account.
Press "Create new app". Name and description are up to you.
In "Redirect URIs" paste exactly the address shown below and save.
Copy the Client ID here. The Client secret is not needed.

string-array.name: setup_steps_deezer
string-array.item: Sign in at developers.deezer.com with your Deezer account and open "My Apps".
Press "Create a new Application". Name and description are up to you.

Deezer only accepts https redirects. A ready-made redirect page is already filled in below: paste that address both in "Application domain" (without https://) and in "Redirect URL after authentication".
Save, then copy the "Application ID" here.

string-array.name: setup_steps_apple
string-array.item: Apple Music needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership ($99 a year) and an Apple Music subscription. Without it, use public playlist links or files.
In "Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles", "Identifiers", create a Media ID with MusicKit enabled.

In "Keys" create a key with "Media Services (MusicKit)" enabled and download the .p8 file (it can be downloaded once). Note the Key ID shown next to it and your Team ID (top right of the account page).
Generate the ES256 developer token (JWT) from the .p8 key: the project README has a ready-made script. Paste the token here.
The token expires after at most six months: when the login stops working, generate a new one and paste it again.

string-array.name: setup_steps_lastfm
string-array.item: Sign in at last.fm and open the API account creation page.
Fill in the form: contact e-mail, application name and description are up to you. "Callback URL" and "Application homepage" can stay empty. Submit.
Copy the "API key" here. The "Shared secret" is not needed.

The pill says how the last run went. Up to date: it finished and nothing waits for you. Removals on hold, Not finished and Not found: N mean something needs a look, and a tap on the pill takes you there. Needs attention: the run failed.
“Not found: 12” opens the review, where you can pick those 12 tracks by hand.

→ is a one-way sync from the source to the target. ↔ marks a two-way pair: two syncs, one per direction, shown as two cards. Editing the ↔ card opens the original sync, and deleting either one deletes both.

Added, removed and not found count the last run: tap a number to see the tracks. Tracks is the size of the source, minus the tracks you ignore; tap it to open the target playlist. The marks below are the recent runs: faded when nothing changed, red when a run failed.
The tracks the last run could not find, plus the matches it was not sure about. You can start fixing them while the sync is still adding, and every choice is remembered for later runs.

▶ runs this sync now, even when it is disabled or set to Wi‑Fi only. Use it after changing a playlist, instead of waiting for the schedule. Large removals are still held back unless you confirmed them in the preview first.
Runs every enabled sync, one after another, ignoring Wi‑Fi only; disabled syncs are skipped. Pulling the list down does the same. While syncs run, a tap on the pill scrolls to the first running card.
With 5 syncs, one of them disabled, 4 run.
The track was matched in an earlier run and is reused without searching again. If that match is wrong, change it in the review: your choice replaces it for every later run.

With only Spotify connected, Step 2 offers Spotify and File, and File is chosen.
Playlists holds your playlists and Liked songs. Library holds saved albums, followed artists, podcasts and, as a source only, recently played. As a target, only playlists you own are listed.

Paste the share link of a public playlist: short links are followed and the name is read. The playlist is only read, never written, so it can\'t be two-way. Some services must be connected even to read a public link.

The playlist is created at the first run, not on Save, and named after the source unless you type a name. If you later delete it on the service, the sync stops and asks you to create it again or pick another.

Runs the sync in the background about every hour, 6 hours, day or week. Android picks the exact moment and may delay it, especially on battery saver. The first run starts within minutes of saving. A scheduled run that finds both playlists unchanged stops at once.

The target becomes a copy of the source: every target track that matches nothing in the source is removed, including tracks you added there yourself. Use it only when the source is your master. If one run would remove more than 10 tracks and over a quarter of the target, they are held back until you confirm them in the preview. Removed tracks can be restored from the Sync log.
Delete a song from your Spotify playlist, and it disappears from the copy at the next run.

After adding, the target is rearranged in the source\'s order; tracks found only in the target move to the end. Skipped for Liked songs and above 1,500 tracks. If the service refuses, the run still succeeds and the Sync log says so.

Off pauses the schedule and leaves the sync out of Sync all, the widget and the tile. You can still run it with ▶ Run now.
How sure Trackhop must be before it adds a track by itself. Strict adds fewer tracks automatically and asks you about more; Loose adds more, with a higher risk of a wrong version.
For a playlist of remixes, Strict avoids picking the radio edit.
Where a service says whether a track is explicit, Trackhop prefers the version you choose. It is a preference, not a filter: if only the other version exists, that one is used.

Connect a service, choose, preview, run.

A sync copies one playlist to another service and keeps it up to date. Four steps:
# 1. Connect
In Accounts, tap Add connector and sign in to the service your music is on. You sign in on the service's own page; Trackhop keeps only an encrypted token on this phone.
# 2. Choose
• Source: a playlist, Liked songs, a Library section (albums, artists) or a public link.
• Target: a service and a new or existing playlist. With only one service connected, the target is a File kept inside Trackhop.
• Options: name, colour, schedule, Mirror removals, Two-way and matching rules. The defaults suit a first sync.
# 3. Preview
Save opens the preview: what would be added, what was not found and the matches to double-check. Settle those with Looks right or Change; the ones you skip are asked about again after the run.
# 4. Run
Tap Run now, then tap the card to follow it track by track. Pause and Stop act between steps. Afterwards the card shows the numbers, and a pill when something needs you: Not found, Removals on hold or Not finished.
What a sync adds, removes or copies back.

# Add only (the default)
The sync only adds. The target can hold extra tracks, and nothing is ever deleted there.
# Mirror removals
The target follows the source, deletions included. Every target track that matches nothing in the source is removed, even one you added there yourself, so use it only when the source is your master.
• Nothing is removed when the source is empty, the search was cut short, or the service can't remove tracks; the Sync log says why.
• If one run would remove more than 10 tracks and over a quarter of the target, the card shows Removals on hold. Tap it to open the preview, check the list, tick Remove these tracks and tap Run now. The tick serves that one run; scheduled runs keep holding back.
• Removed tracks can be put back from Settings › Advanced › Sync log › Restore.
# Two-way
Adds a second sync in the opposite direction, shown as a ↔ card, so tracks added on either side reach the other. Neither half removes anything, so Mirror removals is off: a track deleted on one side usually comes back from the other. Both halves share schedule and rules; editing the ↔ card opens the original sync, and deleting either deletes both.
# Liked songs
With Liked songs as the target, adding a track means liking it, and Mirror removals means unliking the tracks not liked in the source.

# Choosing a schedule
Manual only, Every hour, Every 6 hours, Daily or Weekly. Android picks the exact moment and may delay a run, especially on battery saver.
• The first run starts within minutes of saving, then about once per interval.
• A scheduled run that finds both playlists unchanged stops at once, where the service reports changes.
• Wi‑Fi only makes scheduled runs wait for an unmetered network, usually Wi‑Fi. Run now and Sync all ignore it.
• With Enabled off the schedule pauses; ▶ Run now still works.
# When runs don't happen

In Settings › Syncing, Scheduled syncs not running? opens the list where you exclude Trackhop.\n# Notifications\nYou are told when a scheduled sync adds or removes tracks, and when any sync fails. Turn it off in Settings › Notifications.
See what a run would do, and confirm removals.

The preview shows what a run would do, without changing anything. It opens after you create a sync, or from a card's ⋮ menu › Preview.
# What it lists
• Already on the target, to add, to remove (with Mirror removals only), not found and ignored.
• Matches to double-check: tap Looks right or Change. What you settle is remembered; the rest is asked about again in the review after the run.
• For YouTube, the units the run would use.
To work this out, the preview searches the target for every missing track, so a large playlist takes a while. What it finds is reused by the run.
# Large removals
When a run would remove more than 10 tracks and over a quarter of the target, a red note appears. First check the source: a service that lists a playlist only partly looks exactly like this. If the tracks really should go, tick Remove these tracks and tap Run now. The tick serves only that run, started by hand, and only the tracks you saw; scheduled runs keep holding them back.
# Run now
Runs the sync straight away, reusing what the preview found, so it is much faster than the preview itself.
Find what was missing and check uncertain matches.

# Where to find them
• The Not found pill or the to fix button on a sync card.
• The not found number on the card.
• Settings › Advanced › Sync log › Review.
# Fixing a track
• Proposal: the closest track found, not close enough to add by itself. Tap Add if it is right.
• Search by title, by “artist - title”, or paste a track link from any service. Open in opens the service's own app.
• Likeliest comes first; the source's album, other results and, on YouTube Music, videos are folded below.
• Ask the AI asks your own AI (Settings › Advanced › Your AI) for a better search.
• Ignore stops searching for a track on that service, for every sync to it. There is no undo yet.
Every choice is remembered for later runs. Tracks not found are searched again after a week.
# Uncertain matches
Matches Trackhop was not sure about. Looks right keeps one; Change replaces it, removing the wrong track from the target where the service allows it.
# Matching rules
In the editor, Matching rules set how a track is chosen: Strictness, Explicit versions, Same album and Studio versions only. Exact recording via Deezer (Settings › Syncing) looks up the code that identifies a recording, so Spotify, Apple Music and TIDAL return the exact version.
Keep copies of your playlists and get them back.

# Full backup
Tools › Full backup saves every playlist and the liked songs of one service as dated files in File playlists. The last 5 versions of each playlist are kept, and an unchanged playlist is not written again. Nothing changes on the service.
# Backup to a folder
In Settings › Backups, choose a folder (SD card, a cloud app, any app that offers one). Each run reads every connected service, saves what changed and copies the new files there, so they survive the phone. Choose Manual only, Daily or Weekly, or tap Copy now. On YouTube, reading uses quota.
# Restoring
• A playlist: Tools › File playlists › Import file, pick it from the folder, then make a sync from that file to any service.
• Tracks removed by Mirror removals: Settings › Advanced › Sync log › Restore.
• An unplayable fix: Tools › Unplayable tracks › Undo last fix.
# Export one playlist
Tools › Export a playlist saves it as CSV, M3U, XSPF, JSPF or plain text.

At the top, choose the service the tools work on. A tool it can't do is greyed out.
# Your music
• Trackhop in numbers: what your syncs have done so far.
• Manage playlists: rename, delete, make public or private, look at the tracks.
• Repeats across playlists: tracks in more than one playlist, liked songs in none.
# Move and copy
• Transfer many playlists: one sync per playlist, created and run one after another. They stay in Syncs.
• Export a playlist: one playlist as a file.
• New playlist from…: copy, merge, split, sort or shuffle into a new playlist on the same service. A one-off, not a sync.
• File playlists: imported lists, pasted lists, backups and what syncs wrote to File.
# Clean up
• Remove duplicates: find them, then remove them at once, keeping the first copy.
• Unplayable tracks: swap greyed-out tracks for versions that play, with Undo. Settings can check once a week.
# Share and discover
How compatible are we?, the Playlist poster and the Playlist generator, which uses your own AI.

# Connectors
A connector is one account on one service. Where a service allows it you can add several, for example two Spotify accounts, each with its own name.
# Routes
Some services can be reached two ways. Quick route: you sign in on the service's own page, nothing to create, but it can stop working when the site changes. Official route: the service's own API with a free key in your name; more stable, a few minutes to set up.
In this version the quick routes of Spotify, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, Apple Music and Deezer are built in, and so is SoundCloud with your account. Deezer (web) and SoundCloud are in alpha.

# Your own key
Trackhop ships without keys of its own. The setup guide walks you through the service's developer page: copy the Redirect URI there exactly, then paste the Client ID (and the secret, where asked) here.
• Spotify only lets Premium accounts create a key.
• Apple's developer token expires after six months at most: paste a new one in Settings › Advanced › Service keys.
• On the official YouTube route the daily quota is yours, counted in units.
Your own server (Jellyfin, Plex, Navidrome…) needs its address, your user and a password or token.
# Keeping accounts safe
Passwords are typed on the services' own pages, never in Trackhop. Tokens are encrypted on the phone, and there is no Trackhop server. Test the connection checks a connector; Disconnect deletes its sign-in, and Remove this account also removes the card. Settings › Advanced › Show developer tools › Show connections lists every host the app has contacted.
How separate apps can add services.
Trackhop has an open connector interface: separate apps, made by anyone, can add services to it.

Trackhop does not include, download or recommend any plugin.
• An installed plugin appears in Settings › Plugins, with the services it provides.
• Those services then appear in Accounts › Add connector, like any other.
• Services this version cannot reach on its own are listed as Not available in this version.
• Removing the plugin disconnects its services, and syncs that use them will fail.
In this version the web connectors are built in, so no plugin is needed: every call and every sign-in stays inside Trackhop, and an installed plugin is not used.
